samples.summary: CR_NON_PROSE's closing-fence match is CRLF-intolerant, so on a `\r\n` body no fence is stripped and the bug being fixed returns
samples.evidence:
`const CR_NON_PROSE = /^[ 	]*(`{3,}|~{3,})[\s\S]*?^[ 	]*\1[`~]*[ 	]*$|<!--[\s\S]*?-->/gm;` (harvest.mjs:563). With the `m` flag, `$` matches only immediately before `
`; a closing fence line in a CRLF body is `` ``` `` + `` + `
`, and `[ 	]*` does not consume ``. The fence branch then fails for EVERY fence in the body, `codeRabbitTitle` degrades silently to the old whole-body first-bold behaviour, and a `--glob '!**/node_modules/**'` inside an `rg` transcript becomes the finding's summary again — exactly the defect this change exists to prevent, with no error and no test failure. Every other pattern in this file is CRLF-safe by accident (`CR_LOCATOR` ends `(.*)$` and `.` eats ``; `CR_PROSE_END` and `CR_BLOCKQUOTE_PREFIX` are `^`-anchored only), so this is the one new construct that depends on the line terminator. Bodies come from the live GitHub API (`harvestPr`), not from the checked-in fixtures, and nothing in harvest.mjs normalises line endings (`str` at harvest.mjs:102 only type-checks). Fix: `[ 	]*?$` or normalise `
` in `str`/`codeRabbitTitle`.

samples.summary: codeRabbitTitle is blind to fenced code only, not to the UNFENCED prose inside `🧩 Analysis chain` / `🌐 Web query` blocks, which routinely contains bold and precedes the real title on the 200 comments this change targets
samples.evidence: `codeRabbitTitle` strips only fenced spans and HTML comments (harvest.mjs:563, 578) and deliberately does not stop at `<details>`. CodeRabbit's analysis-chain block contains, besides the shell fences, an unfenced `💡 Result:` narrative for each `🌐 Web query:` — LLM-generated answer text, which habitually uses `**bold**` (e.g. "The latest version is **14.1.0**"). That prose is inside `<details>`, is not fenced, and sits BEFORE the finding's real title in exactly the 200/1588 (12.6%) analysis-chain-first population the docblock at harvest.mjs:521-528 says the design exists to serve. For those bodies the first surviving `**…**` is the web-answer bold, not the title, and the same class of plausible-but-wrong summary reaches the adjudication queue. The test fixture cannot show this: `CR_ANALYSIS_CHAIN_FIRST` states it is 'trimmed in the middle — the web-query text and two more script blocks are cut' (harvest.test.mjs:541-542), i.e. the only content that could exhibit the failure is the content removed.
searchedFor: grep 'Web query|💡 Result|Analysis chain' across repo (only the trimmed fixture and the todo doc match)

samples.summary: The change newly emits `summary: ""` for findings whose only bold span is inside code, and an empty summary is a colliding key (`file::`) that scores 1.00 similarity against every other empty one
samples.evidence: Where the old regex returned markup, `codeRabbitTitle` now returns `""` — the branch's own test pins it: `assert.equal(findings[0].summary, "", "markup was promoted to a title")` (harvest.test.mjs, RV_NO_TITLE_FENCED_GLOB case). `findingKey` is `` `${f.file ?? ""}::${String(f.summary ?? "").toLowerCase().trim()}` `` (scripts/agent/finding-key.mjs:40), so two such findings in one file produce the identical key and `dedupeFindings` collapses them to one record (finding-key.test.mjs:39-54), and `findingSimilarity` scores two empty summaries at 1.00, merging unrelated defects. The docblock at harvest.mjs:569-575 acknowledges this and calls it 'a reason to avoid EMITTING ""' — yet the code has no guard against emitting it and no fallback (e.g. to the first prose sentence marked as derived, or to the locator/detail head) when the code-blind search finds nothing. The task doc's '0 new empty summaries' is a claim about today's corpus only; the constructed fixture shows the shape is reachable.

samples.summary: Replacing a fenced span with "\n" can splice an unclosed `**` before the fence to a `**` after it, so the `/s`-flagged lazy bold match manufactures a title spanning the removed block
samples.evidence: `.replace(CR_NON_PROSE, "\n")` (harvest.mjs:578) followed by `/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/s.exec(prose)` (harvest.mjs:579). The bold regex has the `s` flag and no line bound, so if a body contains an odd `**` in prose above a fence (CodeRabbit does emit `**` in bullet prose) and any `**` below it, the strip brings the two together and the title becomes the concatenation of two unrelated fragments across the excised block — a longer and more plausible-looking wrong summary than the pre-change behaviour, which at least stopped at the first `**` inside the fence. Bounding the bold search to a single line (or to a bounded character count) would remove the class.

samples.summary: The closing-fence tail `[`~]*` accepts a mixed delimiter run, so ```` ```~~~ ```` closes a backtick fence
samples.evidence: `^[ \t]*\1[`~]*[ \t]*$` — after the backreference, the tail character class allows BOTH delimiters, so a line such as ```` ```~~ ```` closes a three-backtick fence even though CommonMark requires the closer to be a run of the SAME character. The test comment at harvest.test.mjs ("the two delimiters cannot be mixed: a `~~~` run must not close a ``` fence") asserts a property the regex does not quite hold — only the leading portion is delimiter-checked. Harmless on today's data; `\1+` (or `[`]*`/`[~]*` selected by the opener) states the intent.

verdict.reason:
The regex at harvest.mjs:563 exists as quoted, but the claimed CRLF-intolerance is based on a false premise about JavaScript regex semantics. Per ECMA-262, the `$` assertion in multiline mode succeeds when the character at the current position is matched by `LineTerminator`, and `LineTerminator` is `<LF> | <CR> | <LS> | <PS>` — `` is itself a line terminator. So on a CRLF closing-fence line "```
", after `\1[`~]*[ 	]*` consumes the fence the cursor sits on ``, and `[ 	]*$` succeeds there; `^` likewise matches after `` and after `
`. The fence branch therefore matches and is stripped on `
` bodies exactly as on `
` bodies, so `codeRabbitTitle` (harvest.mjs:577-580) does not degrade to the old first-bold behaviour and the `rg --glob '!**/node_modules/**'` regression covered by harvest.test.mjs:609-631 does not return. The finding's corroborating claim is wrong the same way: it says `CR_LOCATOR` (harvest.mjs:704) is safe because "`.` eats ``", but in JS `.` does not match ``, precisely because `` is a line terminator. The proposed fix (`[ 	]*?$`) would be a no-op for this pattern.

verdict.reason: The cited code is exactly as the finding describes and I found no guard that makes it unreachable. CR_NON_PROSE (harvest.mjs:563) strips only line-anchored fenced spans and HTML comments; codeRabbitTitle (harvest.mjs:577-579) then takes the first `**…**` anywhere in the remaining body, with no `<details>` boundary — the docblock at harvest.mjs:521-528 states that omission is deliberate. The `CR_PROSE_END` truncation (harvest.mjs:476) is applied only by codeRabbitDetail (harvest.mjs:616), not by the title path. Both callers (harvest.mjs:450 classifyCodeRabbitComment, harvest.mjs:844 parseCodeRabbitReview) pass raw body/span text with no pre-strip of `<details>` interiors, so unfenced prose inside the `🧩 Analysis chain` block reaches the bold search ahead of the real title in exactly the analysis-chain-first population the design targets. The fixture cannot exercise this: harvest.test.mjs:540-543 says the web-query text is cut, and the fixture body (harvest.test.mjs:544-578) contains no `🌐 Web query` / `💡 Result` narrative — its only unfenced non-title lines are "Repository:" and "Length of output:", neither bolded. No corpus of raw CodeRabbit bodies exists in the tree to measure against, and the single live-body check in the task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260812-coderabbit-title-excludes-code-todo.md:194-196) covers one comment only, so it cannot disprove the general shape. Impact if real is a plausible-but-wrong `summary` feeding findingKey/summaryTokens and the adjudication queue — the same class of defect this change exists to fix — which is a correctness-lane logic bug, not out of scope. No named refutation ground available; per the standing rule, uncertainty keeps the finding.
